div.div: Connection reuse removes 480 ms. This is why origin count is a performance decision, and why one preconnect can beat a week of code splitting.

div.div: Brotli · smaller payloads · the first 14 kB matter most

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 758px; height: 1px; padding-top: 454px; margin-left: 38px;

div.div: Every extra origin pays DNS + TCP + TLS again — and cache partitioning means a "shared" CDN copy of a library is no longer shared between sites. Self-host, and preconnect to what is left.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 756px; height: 1px; padding-top: 503px; margin-left: 40px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: var(--dg-warn-fg);

display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans',-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,sans-serif; color: var(--dg-warn-fg); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Split a slow TTFB before you theorise about it: DNS, connect, TLS and server time are four different problems with four different fixes, and the waterfall already tells you which one you have.

a.text: Text is not SVG - cannot display
